summary: [correctness] INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE is answered when no spec root was indexed, which is the usual case (one root with a violation). Real call: a repo with one root whose scenario lacks the provenance line, `canon inventory sync --json` -> exit 1, INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE, reason VIOLATIONS, data.roots[0].written 0, message 'nothing was written for it, and the roots before it are indexed' (there are none), meta.next[0] 'read what `inventory sync` indexed before it stopped: the roots before the unindexed one stay indexed'; `.canon/ledger` was not even created. The brief F3 gives INCOMPLETE to a sync that stopped on a root 'and the earlier roots were indexed' and F1/Acceptance forbid an _INCOMPLETE name with no effect left. The dry-run preview says the same code and the same read-what-was-indexed next although it can never index. Judgment on the dry-run: preview parity with the commit is a defensible reading of ATIP preview-equals-commit and the message does say it was a preview, but the code and next must follow the commit's real outcome. Fix: INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE only when `outcome.roots` has a root with written>0 (commit) -- for a sync that wrote nothing answer the corpus's own failure (a check's finding: exit 1 FAILED-class code with data.roots) with a next that fixes the corpus, and in a preview say 'would be left unindexed' with no read-what-was-indexed next. Scenario atip.incomplete.09 should add the single-root case.
